Q517639.label: 1929 United Kingdom general election
Q517639.desc: general election in the United Kingdom
Q517639.summary: A general election was held in the United Kingdom on Thursday 30 May 1929, after the previous Parliament was dissolved on 10 May. It resulted in a hung parliament: the Conservative Party, led by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin, won the most votes, but Ramsay MacDonald's Labour Party won the most seats in the House of Commons. This marked the first election where Labour emerged as the largest party, though they failed to win a majority. The Liberal Party, led again by former Prime Minister David Lloyd George, regained some of the ground lost in 1924 and held the balance of power.

Q6740999.label: Malagasy constitutional referendum, 1958
Q6740999.summary: A referendum on the new constitution of France was held in Madagascar on 28 September 1958 as part of a wider referendum held across the French Union. The new constitution would see the country become part of the new French Community if accepted, or result in independence if rejected. It was approved by 77.64% of voters. The country subsequently became independent on 26 June 1960.

Q19878919.label: Cameroonian constitutional referendum, 1958
Q19878919.summary: A referendum on the new constitution of France was held in French Cameroons on 28 September 1958 as part of a wider referendum held across the French Union. The new constitution would see the territory become part of the new French Community if accepted, or result in independence if rejected. It was approved by 96.6% of voters.

Q2567.summary: Richard Karl Freiherr von Weizsäcker was a German politician who served as President of Germany from 1984 to 1994. Born into the aristocratic Weizsäcker family, he took his first public offices in the Protestant Church in Germany.

Q1512455.label: 2002 Slovak parliamentary election
Q1512455.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Slovakia on 20 and 21 September 2002. The Movement for a Democratic Slovakia remained the largest party in the National Council, winning 36 of the 150 seats.

Q23559.label: Benito Mussolini
Q23559.summary: Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini was a fascist dictator who was the prime minister of Italy from 1922 until his deposition in 1943. Known as Il Duce during his rule, he established a totalitarian dictatorship led by the National Fascist Party (PNF) in the Kingdom of Italy.

Q2633735.label: 2001 Cypriot legislative election
Q2633735.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cyprus on 27 May 2001. The result was a victory for AKEL, which won 20 of the 56 seats. Voter turnout was 91.8%.

Q22662663.label: 2016 Kaohsiung earthquake
Q22662663.desc: deadly earthquake centered north of Pingtung City, Taiwan
Q22662663.summary: At 03:57 local time on 6 February 2016, an earthquake with a moment magnitude of 6.4 struck 28 km (17 mi) northeast of Pingtung City in southern Taiwan, in the Meinong District of Kaohsiung. The earthquake struck at a depth of around 23 km (14 mi). Its comparatively shallow depth caused more intense reverberations on the surface.

Q1150983.label: one-state solution
Q1150983.desc: proposed resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict involving a single state with both Israelis and Palestinians as citizens
Q1150983.summary: The one-state solution is a proposed approach to the Israeli–Palestinian peace process that envisions a single state within the boundaries of the former Mandatory Palestine, standing in contrast to the two-state solution. It is sometimes described as a bi-national state, reflecting the idea that it could provide self-determination to Israelis and Palestinians within a shared state. The term one-state reality refers to the view that the current situation in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict amounts to a single de facto political space.

Q18127879.label: Marxism–Leninism–Maoism
Q18127879.desc: political ideology based on Marxism–Leninism and Maoism
Q18127879.summary: Marxism–Leninism–Maoism (MLM) is a term used by some communist groups to emphasize the significance of Maoism as a new stage in Marxist theory and practice. Adherents of Marxism–Leninism–Maoism claim it to be a unified, coherent higher stage of Marxism. The term is sometimes used interchangeably with "Maoism" and "Marxism–Leninism" by adherents, although the latter term is more associated with Stalinism.
